title: A Lease-End Timeline: What to Do 120, 90, 60, 30 and 7 Days Out
description: A countdown of tasks for the last four months of a lease, so nothing is left to the final week.
body:
Last-minute lease decisions cost money. Quotes expire, appointments book up, and financing takes time. Spread the work across four months and each step is small.

120 days out: gather

  • Locate your lease contract. If you cannot find it, request a copy.
  • Write down the end date, allowed miles, and your current odometer.
  • Note your monthly payment so you know what a replacement car must beat.
  • Decide what matters most: keeping this car, getting a different one, or spending less.

90 days out: learn the numbers

  • Read the lease-end letter. Our line-by-line guide helps.
  • Call for a payoff quote using the call script.
  • Estimate market value from at least three sources.
  • Calculate any mileage overage in both directions.

60 days out: choose a direction

  • Compare buy, return, and extend. Extending can be useful if a replacement car is not ready, and we cover it in Extending Your Lease Instead.
  • If buying, start your financing conversation and confirm the leasing company's requirements.
  • If returning, schedule the free pre-inspection if one is offered.

30 days out: execute

  • Submit applications and documents. Respond quickly to requests for more information.
  • Re-confirm the payoff amount and its expiration date.
  • Arrange insurance changes if you will own the car.
  • If returning, make repairs or collect repair quotes, and arrange your next vehicle.

7 days out: close the loop

  • Confirm the payment method and timing with whoever is sending funds.
  • Photograph the car and record the final mileage.
  • Remove personal items, toll tags, and saved data from the infotainment system.
  • Collect all keys and accessories.

The day after

Confirm that the lessor has recorded the payoff or the return. Ask when to expect a title or a final account statement. Cancel or update automatic payments so you are not charged again for a lease that has ended.

If you are already late

Start at the 30-day section and do the earliest items in parallel: call for the payoff, check market value, and ask about extension options. A short extension can buy time to do the rest properly.
